description: 2 tactical challenges for White against the Albin Countergambit. Meet 2...e5 with accurate play and neutralize the d4 wedge.

drills.briefExplanation: 2.c4 e5 3.dxe5 d4 4.Nf3 Nc6 5.g3 — accept the pawn, challenge the wedge, and fianchetto against it.
drills.description: White to play. Black may try the Albin 2...e5 — offer the gambit and be ready.
drills.explanation: 2.c4 invites the Albin, and White should accept the challenge: 3.dxe5 wins the pawn, and after 3...d4 4.Nf3 develops while attacking the wedge. 4...Nc6 5.g3 prepares the fianchetto — the bishop on g2 will stare down the long diagonal at the d4 pawn for the rest of the game. White's plan: complete development, play e3 at the right moment, and prove the extra pawn matters.
drills.name: Holding the Extra Pawn

drills.briefExplanation: 4.Nf3 Nc6 5.g3 Nge7 6.Bg2 Ng6 7.O-O Be6 8.b3 — develop around the wedge and prepare the e3 break.
drills.description: White to play. The d4 wedge is established — develop solidly and prepare to undermine it.
drills.explanation: Against the wedge, White plays around it, not through it. 4.Nf3 attacks d4 immediately, and after 4...Nc6 5.g3 Nge7 White continues 6.Bg2 Ng6 7.O-O — king safe, rook coming to e1. 7...Be6 8.b3 prepares Bb2, when White's bishops both aim at Black's center and the e3 break will dissolve the wedge on White's terms.
drills.name: Blunting the Wedge

name: Albin Countergambit — White Tactics
